title: Queued-token scarcity safeguard and graceful backpressure strategy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem summary: under sustained high QPS we observe a mode where GPU token slots are effectively exhausted by a small number of long-context or high-token requests that enter micro-batches. This causes short, latency-sensitive requests to be delayed by multiple batch cycles (up to 3–5x target p95) despite idle compute headroom for short paths. Root cause hypothesis: token-slot scarcity (KV + transient token allocations) combined with first-come-first-serve microbatch admission allows long requests to monopolize batch composition and KV residency, and our current admission controller lacks per-length awareness and aging eviction for KV entries.
background: SRE/observability flagged recurring customer incidents in Monday 2026-02-02 where a high-traffic checkout endpoint saw p95 jump from 60ms to 420ms during a batch of 120 concurrent sessions. Dashboards show GPU memory headroom was not the limiting factor; instead token-slot accounting and KV cache hit-rate oscillations preceded the latency spike. Existing tickets focus on admission thresholds and headroom predictors (see ENG-30210, ENG-31577) but investigation shows a different pattern: a small fraction of requests with long context dominate the microbatch windows, inflating per-batch token counts and pushing our token gating into conservative backpressure mode. This ticket aims to add a targeted safeguard that prioritizes short requests and protects latency SLAs while retaining throughput for bulk workloads.
proposed_solution: Design and implement a queued-token scarcity safeguard made of three coordinated components: (1) short-request fastpath and token-slot reservation: reserve a configurable fraction of per-GPU token budget for requests below a configurable token-length threshold (eg. <=256 tokens). (2) soft preemption / token leasing: allow short, queued requests to preempt a fraction of microbatch slots by leasing token slots from long requests using a time-bounded lease; leases revert if long request makes progress. (3) aging-based KV eviction and ephemeral prefix promotion: mark KV entries created by long-running sessions as `ephemeral` with lower residency weight; promote short-request prefixes to higher retention during scarcity. Admission controller will expose signal metrics and a debug mode for stepwise rollout. This is designed to be compatible with existing batchers and KV reclamation paths and to avoid global throttles that reduce throughput for all customers.
work_done:
- PoC simulator implemented to model token-slot competition across 3 request length classes (short/medium/long) and microbatch windows. Simulator shows p95 for short requests improves by ~3x at 90th percentile traffic with <5% impact to aggregate throughput.
- Implemented admission control flags and metrics in runtime branch `feature/queued-token-guard` (internal PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1823).
- Added prefix-level KV residency tag `ephemeral` and eviction weight hooks (runtime PR linked).
- Canary run on staging (us-west-2) across 6 GPUs with synthetic mix (70% short, 25% medium, 5% long) for 2 hours: short-request p95 reduced from 360ms to 120ms during peak; KV miss-rate increased 2 percentage points but overall token cost dropped 6%.
open_items:
- Finalize token-reservation default and knob bounds (experimentation suggests 8–15% reserved works well but needs validation across customer mixes).
- Integrate soft-lease telemetry into Console traces and add rollout toggles per-dedicated-pool.
- Add integration tests to catch regressions where preemption could starve long streaming generation (ensure progress guarantees).
- Policy: define billing/observability for preempted requests (should not double-charge or drop metrics).
- Security review: confirm no information leakage via KV eviction ordering under multi-tenant Dedicated pools (short term marked as false but we'll request a scoped review).
tradeoffs_and_decisions:
- Reservation vs. dynamic prioritization: reservation is simple and predictable; dynamic prioritization (score-based) yields slightly higher throughput but is harder to reason about for SLOs. We selected a conservative reservation default with ability to switch to score-based in high-throughput pools.
- Soft preemption complexity: introduces lease bookkeeping and potential fairness edge-cases; chosen approach is time-bounded leases to minimize starvation risk.
- KV eviction weighting: promoting short prefixes increases short-request hit-rate but may increase churn. We avoid hard guarantees and instead expose a tunable eviction multiplier per pool.
metrics_and_slos: Proposed metrics to track after rollout: token_slot_utilization (per-GPU), short_request_p95, short_request_p99, kv_hit_rate_by_prefix_length, lease_preemptions_per_minute, aggregate_throughput_tps. SLO objective: maintain short_request_p95 <= 200ms for dedicated pools with configured reservation enabled under 95th percentile QPS observed in the pool.

testing_plan:
- Unit tests for lease lifecycle and slot accounting.
- Integration tests with microbatch simulator to assert short-request p95 under synthetic mixes.
- Staged canary rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100% across dedicated pools, monitor token_slot_utilization and short_request_p99 for regressions.
- Chaos test: inject a flood of long-context requests and measure preemption fairness.
rollback_plan: Disable reservation flag and revert admission hook (runtime feature flag). Re-enable previous headroom predictor. If KV eviction churn causes errors, revert KV residency tag change and rely on previous eviction heuristics. All changes behind rollout flags and incremental canary so rollback is single-platform feature-flag flip.
acceptance_criteria:
- Short-request p95 improvement confirmed on staging with representative QPS mix and no >10% throughput degradation.
- Telemetry surfaces lease_preemptions and per-GPU reservation consumption.
- No customer-facing errors introduced in canary; post-canary for 24h with no SEV>1 incidents.
- Docs updated: Runtime admission controller section and Console runbook.
notes: This ticket aims to be surgical: protect latency-sensitive paths without broadly constraining throughput. If successful, follow-ups include per-tenant reservation, ML-driven reservation adaptation, and an A/B experiment to compare reservation vs. scoring policies.
